job.value: Check the card and current bid, then place a bid

arrivedFrom.value: a timed-auction card on web Homepage, SERP or Event page

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The card gallery, 'Mew 030/028', 'S$620 2 bids', the countdown and the bid box make it an auction listing.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The bid box is prominent, but 'Place bid' is grey-disabled until an amount is entered, so the quick-pick '630 / 650 / 670' chips carry the visual weight.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'One-time bid' / 'Max bid', the 'Your bid' field and amount chips predict their effect.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'Max bid' is introduced next to 'One-time bid' but only the one-time option is explained in the visible line.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Choosing between 'One-time bid' and 'Max bid' up front asks a first-time bidder for a strategy decision before they've placed any bid.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: The terms line ('Winning bids are binding...') belongs there, but the bid-type choice could be tucked behind the field.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Every element serves evaluating and bidding on this card.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: The mode line and the binding-bids terms paragraph sit between the field and the button, so there's text to get through before bidding.
